To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there is little evidence that the UK National Health service primary care reforms have improved the health of the population or the efficiency of the health service.

the UK general practice funding system, the general practitioner (GP) contract and the Health Of the Nation targets have not been subject of adequate evaluation, the evidence base regarding the clinical effectiveness and cost effectiveness of interventions delivered in primary care is inadequate and the knowledge base regarding how behaviour change in general practitioners can be achieved and how cost effective interventions can be adopted in routine clinical practice is inadequate.

The system of primary health care in the United Kingdom appears to have become a popular model amongst policy makers worldwide, but there is a paucity of evidence to suggest that this system is either effective or cost-effective.

the following: 1) The development of a knowledge base to inform the delivery of effective primary medical care; 2) The development of methods of assessing the cost effectiveness of interventions in primary care; 3) The development of strategies to improve the adoption of effective interventions in primary care.

the evaluation of health services and the improvement of the knowledge base on which policy is made.

the UK system of primary care is a model to be avoided.
the evidence base for policy decisions regarding primary care is poor and the need for research is great.
